The manufacturers are all in on the bullet energy thing, (Mass squared x velocity = energy) but it was pointed out that a lot of the times this doesn't work. The Taylor Knock Out index is based upon real world experiences. John "Pondoro" Taylor was a famous African big game poacher and hunter. He developed a theory that differed from bullet energy because the bullet energy didn't mean squat when taking a large animal. What Taylor said was that bullet diameter was also a factor in Taking out a animal. So the Taylor theory that (Mass of the bullet X the velocity of the bullet X the diameter of the bullet divided by 7000 (number of grains in a pound)) yielded the relative knock out power of a cartridge.

So what Taylor was advocating was that a bigger slower moving large diameter projectile was more deadly than a lighter smaller diameter high velocity projectile. There is some real world proof of this as a bigger much slower moving projectile (say a .45-70 projectile ) is more deadly than a smaller bullet moving at a much higher velocity.

So this argument is also portrayed in the endless argument of which is better the 9mm parabellum or the .45 ACP for knocking down a intruder. To bring this down to real world lets look a a body of water. which makes a bigger splash. as small rock thrown at high velocity into a pond of water or a big huge rock thrown at a much lower velocity. The larger in diameter of a slower moving projectile displaces more water on impact than a projectile of the same weight moving at a higher velocity.
